scenes.vo: [smug, theatrical] At one big US veterans' hospital, the no-show rate averaged eighteen point two percent in the four years before reminder letters. In the four years after: seventeen. Hi again. Empty chair. Barely noticed.
scenes.label: no-show rate, 4 years before vs after reminder letters (one US VA hospital)
scenes.visual: The chair from BL #4 turns around, unbothered; an envelope lands next to it

scenes.vo: Same hospital in Houston. Twelve years of records.
[delighted] And when researchers compared the year before and after, month by month, the change wasn't even statistically significant.
scenes.visual: Two calendars side by side, the bars nearly level

scenes.vo: The researchers said reminders only modestly reduced no-shows. I call them a nice try.
Because a reminder doesn't fill my seat. Somebody else does.
scenes.visual: A second figure waits at the door

scenes.vo: [nervous] What actually scares me? A one-tap way to cancel or rebook, so someone else gets the slot.
scenes.visual: Phone shows Cancel / Rebook; the waiting figure sits down; the chair panics

scenes.vo: [smug, recovering] Anyway. I'll save you a seat. And remember:
